questions.q: Why does Finance get a VIEW on top of refund_events instead of a separate copy table?
options: A separate copy table would be identical, so the choice doesn't matter
A view is a saved query with no storage of its own, so it automatically reflects refund_events' latest data with no refresh step
Views are required by Snowflake whenever a table has a VARIANT column
Tables cannot be queried by Power BI, only views can
questions.explain: A view re-runs its query every time it's selected from, so it always reflects the current state of refund_events without any manual refresh.

questions.q: Why does vw_finance_refunds aggregate to subscriber + week, instead of exposing raw refund_events rows directly?
options: Snowflake views cannot return more than one row per subscriber
Raw refund_events rows are stored in a format Power BI cannot read
Finance's real question is about refund totals by subscriber and week, not individual raw events
Aggregation is required before any view can be created in Snowflake
questions.explain: The view is shaped to match how Finance will actually use the data, aggregating individual refund events up to a useful grain.

questions.q: Why does this lesson include refund_event_count in the view alongside total_refund_amount?
options: It has no real purpose and could be removed
Power BI requires at least two numeric columns in every view
It's a deliberate sanity-check column — an unexpectedly high count makes a wrong total easier to spot without digging into the raw table
It's needed to satisfy a Snowflake syntax requirement for GROUP BY
questions.explain: refund_event_count is the same kind of diagnostic number Lesson 13 later uses to spot the chapter's bug.

questions.q: What does DATE_TRUNC('week', updated_at) do in this view's GROUP BY?
options: Buckets each refund event's updated_at timestamp down to the start of its week
Filters out any event older than one week
Deletes the updated_at column from the result
Converts updated_at to a VARIANT type
questions.explain: DATE_TRUNC('week', ...) rounds a timestamp down to the start of its week, which is the grouping grain this view uses.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend writing down the current total_refund_amount and refund_event_count now, in Lesson 8?
options: Snowflake requires a manual baseline before any view can be queried by Power BI
It's a baseline you'll compare against when Lesson 13's numbers stop matching
The numbers will be deleted automatically after 24 hours
It has no bearing on later lessons — it's just good general practice
questions.explain: Lesson 13 reproduces a reported discrepancy, and having a known-good baseline from this lesson makes that reproduction concrete rather than vague.
